core_obligations: Show that the section s is quasi-compact using the permanence lemma and the quasi-compactness of V -> Y (proof lines 3393-3394).
Use that the scheme theoretic image commutes with restriction to opens to identify Y' intersect f^{-1}(V) with the image of the restricted section (proof lines 3395-3398).
Apply that a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion (proof lines 3398-3402).
Conclude that Y' -> Y is an isomorphism over V (proof lines 3402-3404).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a separated morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, an open subspace V with V -> Y quasi-compact and a section s : V -> X of f over V, the scheme theoretic image Y' of s is an isomorphism over V (source lines 3382-3390). The proof shows that s is quasi-compact by the permanence statement, hence the construction of the scheme theoretic image commutes with restriction to opens; therefore Y' intersect f^{-1}(V) is the scheme theoretic image of a section of the separated morphism f^{-1}(V) -> V, and since a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion, that image map is an isomorphism.
